The EU's digital wallet is a double-blind claims verification system.

Service provider asks you to prove a claim - e.g. whether you're 18+ - and only gets back a token answering yes/no to that claim, which is cryptographically signed by your government. That token is relayed through your own computing device which means the government only sees you retrieving a token, but is not privy to who will receive it; while the service provider only receives a token with the answer to the claim and not any actual identity information that would allow trace-back to your realworld self.

All of the code and protocols handling this are open source and have been vetted as not containing any shenanigans such as surreptitious additional marks allowing token's to be correlated at a later time.

looked at the actual study

It was a retrospective cohort study that tracked 10,000's of patients on GLP-1 RA (ozempic) vs a drug-free control group matched for age, BMI, comorbidities etc. then followed up their risk of osteoporosis + others at 5 years.

Obviously the flaw with this study is that being fat itself is a well known protective factor against osteoporosis (added weight that stresses the skeleton drives osteoclast processes to strengthen the bones), so implicating the drug is pre-emptive unless a better study or analysis can actually control for the fact that thinner people are more likely to develop brittle bones AND that people on ozempic are more likely to lose more weight than controls.

And even if that gets controlled for, the next most obvious answer is that people losing weight without ozempic might be more likely to be doing exercise which strengthens bones and prevents osteoporosis as well.

These are 2 big hurdles you need to clear before accusing the drug itself of interfering with bone activity directly - especially when there is no obviously biological/receptor pathway that can currently be implicated. And it can be absolutely done with a better study that works prospectively to track the patient cohort data as they lose weight and exercise over time.

For now, I believe the vast majority of doctors are simply going to ignore this like most other clickbait articles online.
